1) Decision — Restate: Decide how to implement a simple server-rendered Team Dashboard route, backend handler, and DB query that shows item title, status, assignee, and due date with a status filter, fitting into the existing web app/backend/relational DB without adding new services.  
2) Assumptions & constraints — Using the current single server-rendered web app, one backend service, and a relational DB; no new services/databases; small JS is permitted for filtering; the page is a lightweight single view used a few times/day; tenant scoping is required so users only see their org's teams/items and raw numeric IDs must not be exposed.  
3) Options considered — (A) Server-rendered, server-side filtered SQL query per request (minimal JS triggers page GETs with status query param); (B) Server-rendered fetch-all active items once and apply client-side JS filtering; (C) Server-rendered with in-app short-lived per-tenant/team cache to reduce DB load.  
4) Trade-offs — (A) is simplest, keeps access control in one place, supports pagination and predictable DB cost but increases query volume under load; (B) can be snappier for tiny teams and fewer DB hits but risks overfetching sensitive data and scales poorly; (C) reduces DB cost but adds invalidation/staleness complexity and testing surface; all options should use parameterized queries, WHERE tenant_id = current_tenant, and avoid emitting raw DB IDs (use per-tenant slugs or signed/opaque IDs).  
5) Recommendation & follow-ups — Recommend (A): add a server route (e.g., /teams/:team_slug/dashboard or /dashboard?team=<signed_id>), backend handler that verifies tenant membership, runs a parameterized JOIN to return only (title,status,assignee_name,due_date) with status filter and sensible LIMIT/pagination, and use minimal JS to re-request with status changes; follow-ups: confirm auth provides tenant_id and membership checks, decide slug vs signed-id strategy, agree max items/pagination limits, confirm acceptable assignee PII exposure, and any latency/SLA targets to tune DB queries.

5) Recommendation & monitoring/follow-ups — Use (B): (i) Counts: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM workflow_items WHERE tenant_id = :t AND team_id = :team [AND assignee_id = :assignee][AND other_filters] GROUP BY status; (ii) Rows (choose prepared statement per sort to preserve index use): for due_date sort run SELECT wi.title, wi.status, wi.assignee_id, u.display_name AS assignee_name, wi.due_date FROM workflow_items wi LEFT JOIN users u ON wi.assignee_id = u.id WHERE wi.tenant_id = :t AND wi.team_id = :team [AND wi.status = :status][AND wi.assignee_id = :assignee] ORDER BY wi.due_date ASC LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset; for last_updated sort use ORDER BY wi.updated_at DESC LIMIT/OFFSET using the other prepared statement; (iii) Index tweaks: add/ensure composite indexes (tenant_id, team_id, status, due_date, id) and (tenant_id, team_id, status, updated_at, id) and optionally (tenant_id, team_id, assignee_id, status, due_date) and a lower(display_name) or trigram index for assignee searches; (iv) Observability: instrument per-request metrics and DB span timings, capture separate histograms for counts query and rows query, enable slow-query logging and EXPLAIN-based checks in staging, set alerts (example thresholds: P95 request or DB query > 400ms or error rate >1% or >X concurrent dashboard requests causing queueing), and run periodic EXPLAIN/pg_stat_statements reviews; follow-ups: run EXPLAIN on staging with representative params, confirm DB engine/version and current index/cardinality, agree alert thresholds, and confirm assignee filter UX (ID vs free-text) so we can finalize indexes and prepared statements.
